newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah stable, swaps up on liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah stable, swaps up on liquidity.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah was stable against the dollar in slow late trading on Friday, with swap rates seen trending up on tight liquidity, dealers said.
They said trading had slowed down and short dollar covering pushed the rupiah a touch lower.
One U.S. bank dealer said there were some dollar purchases by London operators in the afternoon, but a tight rupiah market seemed to limit the upside.
Another foreign bank dealer said calmer regional markets helped slow Jakarta trading, with the focus on Thailand's economic rescue plan to be released next week.
Spot rupiah was at 2,608/12 at 0930 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,613/23. Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,607.5/11.5 and 2,608.25/10.25, respectively.
"Sentiment is a bit bullish on the dollar. But further uptrend is capped with operators looking to cash out from higher levels," the U.S. bank dealer said.
He said swaps were biddish on the back of increased tightening in the money market. Overnight money ended at 20 percent, with short-dated swaps suggesting a further uptrend.
Overnight swap was at 1.3/1.4 and tom/next at 0.45/0.55.
One local bank dealer said the central bank continued with its tight grip on the rupiah by raising four-to-six day bilateral papers (SBIs) by 300 basis points to 15.0 percent.
The central bank kept short-term rates high to contain speculative dollar buying, dealers said.
The central bank scrapped the offer of repo purchases and remained absent from the short-term securities (SBPUs) market.

The bank offered three-day bilateral SBIs at 14.0 percent, four-to-six day at 15.0 percent, one-week at 10.0 percent, two-week at 10.5 percent, one-month at 11.125 percent, three at 11.0, six at 11.625 and one-year at 12.25 percent.
Dealers said the central bank was likely to maintain high short-term rates as the foreign exchange market continued to fluctuate in response to regional currency instability.
One-month swap was at 18.0/18.5, two at 35.0/40.0, three at 55.0/59.0 and six at 114.0/119.0 points.
The central bank kept its intervention band at 2,378/2,682 but raised the conversion band to 2,585/2,633 on Friday from 2,575/2,623 on Thursday.
